After the golden eagles were removed and the feral pigs were eradicated, captive-bred foxes were released back into the wild. With fewer predators and competing land animals, the population grew quickly. National Park Service surveys showed that the number of foxes increased from fewer than 70 in 2004 to about 2,100 by 2015. Similar recoveries took place on nearby San Miguel and Santa Rosa islands, where fox populations had also been severely reduced by golden eagle predation.In August 2016, the US department of the interior held a formal announcement to mark the removal of the Santa Cruz, San Miguel, and Santa Rosa island fox subspecies from the Federal List of Threatened and Endangered Wildlife. The recovery was recognized as the fastest recovery of any mammal listed under the Endangered Species Act since the law was passed in 1973. "The Island Fox recovery is an incredible success story about the power of partnerships and the ability of collaborative conservation to correct course for a species on the brink of extinction," US Interior secretary Sally Jewell said during the delisting announcement. Former U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Director Dan Ashe also highlighted the achievement, noting that in 2004 the foxes had been given a 50 percent chance of becoming extinct within the next decade. By 2016, three of the four subspecies had recovered, while the fourth was also improving. National Park Service Director Jon Jarvis stressed the importance of the emergency captive-rearing program. He said that captive breeding was critical to saving the foxes and that restoring balance to the island ecosystem helped secure their survival. After the federal delisting, the National Park Service and The Nature Conservancy continued conservation work and introduced biosecurity measures at visitor access points. Island managers continue to monitor fox health, screen for diseases, and control the movement of animals and materials from mainland boat harbours to prevent non-native animals and harmful pathogens from reaching Santa Cruz Island.
Article Summary: Feral pigs brought to the island as domestic animals in the 19th century became wild and formed large populations. The large number of pigs attracted non-native golden eagles from mainland California. As a result, the fox population fell by more than 90 percent. In August 2016, three subspecies of the Channel Islands fox were removed from the endangered species list.

Article Title: America's Lake Powell reaches record low, experts warn against propping; Utah Governor says it's not time to let the lake go
Article Text:
Lake Powell reaches historic low in August

What happens if the water level goes down further

No, it's not time to let Lake Powell go

Propping up Lake Powell is not a long-term solution: Experts

Lake Powell has fallen to a record-low elevation, 20 feet lower than it was at the beginning of 2026. The decline is not unexpected as scientists have been warning against this approaching doom. Lake Powell is the second-largest man-made reservoir in the YS by totak capacity, second to Lake Mead downstream.Situated primarily within San Juan, Kane, and Garfield counties in Utah, with its southern tip anchored in Coconino County, Arizona, Lake Powell was created by the impoundment of the Colorado River via the massive Glen Canyon Dam. Extending roughly 186 miles upstream into deep sandstone canyons, Lake Powell sits at the heart of the Colorado River Basin system, serving as the critical hydrological junction between the Upper Basin states of Colorado, Utah, Wyoming, and New Mexico, and the Lower Basin states of Arizona, California, and Nevada, as well as Mexico.Lake Mead also reached its historic low, straining the Colorado River System.Salt Lake Tribune reported that the reclamation bureau Friday released its two-year operating plan. According to it, the Trump administration won’t force Utah and other Upper Basin states to cut their Colorado River water use over the next two years, but Lower Basin states like California will collectively slash their consumption by over 1 million acre-feet per year.A "24-Month Study" published in April 2026 estimated that Lake Powell could decline below 3,490 feet in August without major intervention. The Bureau of Reclamation has already taken steps intended to stabilize Lake Powell. Earlier this year, the agency said it planned to move as much as 2.48 million acre-feet of water into Powell by reducing releases from the reservoir and drawing on water from upstream Flaming Gorge Reservoir. Reclamation projected that the steps taken could raise Powell's elevation to an estimated 3,500 feet by April 2027.Glen Canyon Dam's hydroelectric turbines require the reservoir to remain above approximately 3,490 feet, known as the minimum power pool. Powell is now only about 30 feet above that threshold. If the reservoir falls below it, Glen Canyon Dam would no longer be able to generate hydropower through its turbines.The Colorado River Basin experienced prolonged drought and increasing temperatures, which eventually led to the present situation.Utah Governor Spencer Cox said it's definitely not time to let Lake Powell go. "What I will say is we have a framework with the Department of Interior. You all have seen it, you all have reported on it. We need to keep Lake Powell from hitting deadpool. That's important. There are really hard sacrifices that every state has to make as we move forward with preserving the Colorado." he said.Since Lake Powell needs a minimum level to keep generating power, the Reclamation Bureau brings water from Flaming Gorge to sustain Lake Powell. But Flaming Gorge takes a severe hit, dropping its surface elevation by as much as 25 to 35 feet and reducing its total capacity from around 82% down to 59%. This creates major disruptions for local tourism and regional economies in Utah and Wyoming, leaving boat ramps high and dry and forcing marinas to relocate docks further into the receding reservoir. Experts feel this can't be a permanent solution.This band-aid solution also affects the water supplies in the Lower Basin states of California, Nevada and Arizona and a push for conservation in the Upper Basin states of Utah, Wyoming, New Mexico and Colorado
Article Summary: Lake Powell has fallen to a record-low elevation, 20 feet lower than it was at the beginning of 2026. Lake Powell is the second-largest man-made reservoir in the YS by totak capacity, second to Lake Mead downstream. Lake Mead also reached its historic low, straining the Colorado River System.

Article Title: ‘Scapegoating mob behavior’: Trump official slams Ghent over US academic Nathan Cofnas suspension
Article Text:
Nathan Cofnas (L), who exposed Cambridge professor Jason Arday’s plagiarism, suspended by Ghent University.

US mission condemns 'retaliation'

Suspension follows Arday controversy

US Ambassador to Belgium Bill White has publicly condemned Ghent University's suspension of American academic Nathan Cofnas, who had exposed alleged plagiarism in the work of late Cambridge professor Jason Arday, with the US mission saying it was reviewing its relationship with the university.The intervention came after Cofnas announced on X that he had been suspended by Ghent University and expected to be fired. He said the action was ordered by university rector Petra De Sutter.In a strongly worded statement, the US Mission to Belgium described the suspension as retaliation against an American scholar following what it called his “accurate whistleblower reporting on academic fraud”.The mission said the US government regularly funds and supports research, academic exchanges and other engagements with overseas universities and was therefore reviewing any relationships it had with Ghent University.“Dishonest, corrupt institutions that engage in, or reward, scapegoating mob behavior are not desirable partners for us,” the statement said.It also defended Cofnas on free speech grounds, saying controversial views were protected and that his academic views had been known to Ghent University when he was hired.The move followed Cofnas's detailed July analysis of Arday's academic work, in which he alleged that parts of the late professor's 2015 PhD thesis closely matched earlier academic material, including work by other scholars.Arday acknowledged citation errors but denied intentional academic misconduct, attributing problems with his doctoral work to inadequate supervision and his autism.The allegations prompted wider scrutiny of Arday's academic record. Cambridge University later announced an investigation into his qualifications and honorary appointments, after which Arday resigned. He was subsequently found dead on August 14.On August 19, Ghent University said it was taking Cofnas's recent public statements about the Arday case “very seriously” and would take “appropriate action within its powers and the applicable framework”.The university did not specify what Cofnas was accused of doing and said it would not prejudge the outcome of the matter, citing the confidentiality of the personnel process.Cofnas joined Ghent University as a postdoctoral researcher in 2026. His appointment had already attracted criticism from some staff and students over his views on hereditarianism and differences between groups.
Article Summary: US mission condemns'retaliation' against American academic Nathan Cofnas. US Ambassador to Belgium Bill White publicly condemned Ghent University's suspension of American academic. C ofnas had exposed alleged plagiarism in the work of late Cambridge professor Jason Arday.

Article Title: In 1922, an American engineer built a house from more than 100,000 newspapers; 100 years later the paper walls still survive
Article Text:
PC: wikipedia

How an American engineer built the 1922 newspaper house

PC: wikipedia

More than 100,000 newspapers were used to build the paper house

How old newspapers were turned into tables, chairs, lamps and clocks

How the newspaper house survived for more than a century

In 1922, an American engineer began building a summer house in Rockport, Massachusetts, with an unusual material in mind: old newspapers. Elis F. Stenman was interested in whether discarded pages could do more than carry the day's news, so he began pressing and bonding them into the walls of his house. What started as an experiment with paper insulation gradually spread through the building. More than 100,000 newspapers were eventually used, with flour-based glue holding layers together and varnish helping protect them from moisture. The wooden frame remained the house's structural backbone, but paper became its defining feature. Stenman later made furniture and household objects from newspapers, leaving printed headlines and advertisements visible in parts of the interior. More than a century later, the Rockport Paper House remains an unusual record of an engineer's attempt to turn a material normally discarded within days into something built to last.It is easy to imagine the Rockport house as a building made entirely from newspaper, but that is not quite how Stenman's experiment worked. The basic skeleton was conventional. Wood provided the frame, while the newspaper was used mainly in the walls and other parts of the interior.That distinction matters because the paper was never expected to perform every job required of a building.Stenman began work on the summer house in 1922. According to a report by Click Petróleo e Gás, a news portal based in Brazil, the engineer was interested in the insulating qualities of paper and began collecting large quantities of old newspapers. Rather than using individual sheets as thin coverings, he built up layers of them, bonding the pages together until they formed substantial sections.The walls were made from repeated layers rather than a single thick sheet. 215 layers of paper in the walls. Seen from outside, the result could still resemble a fairly ordinary small house, but inside, the newspapers remained visible. Headlines, advertisements and pieces of articles were left embedded in the walls instead of being covered completely.There was also an unexpected benefit to leaving the pages exposed. The building became a record of the period in which it was made. The newspapers were no longer simply building material; they carried pieces of the news and commercial life of the 1920s with them.The scale of Stenman's project becomes clearer when the number of newspapers is considered. More than 100,000 newspapers were eventually used. That meant countless individual pages had to be collected, arranged and bonded before they could become part of the house.The adhesive was homemade. Flour was used as the basis of the glue, helping the sheets stick together as they were built up in layers. Once compressed and bonded, the paper was considerably different from the loose pages people would normally associate with a newspaper. The walls then received another layer of protection. Varnish was applied to the newspaper surfaces, helping to reduce the effect of moisture and exposure. This was particularly important in Rockport, a coastal Massachusetts town where a paper structure would otherwise have faced an obvious problem.The arrangement also explains why the house could survive for so long. The newspapers were not simply left in their original, vulnerable form. They were part of a combination involving the wooden frame, tightly packed paper, adhesive and protective coating. The survival of the house does not mean newspapers became a general replacement for conventional construction. The paper served particular purposes within a larger structure.Stenman's use of newspaper did not stop once the walls were complete. The same material began appearing throughout the interior, where it was turned into objects that would normally have been made from wood or other materials.The house came to contain newspaper tables, chairs, lamps, shelves and clocks. Rolled sheets could be treated almost like narrow wooden sections, then cut and assembled into furniture. Some objects retained the printed pages in a way that made their original purpose obvious. That makes the interior rather different from a conventional recycled-material project. The newspaper is not merely hidden inside a wall. In places, the words and pictures remain part of the finished object.Other unusual details associated with the house include paper-covered household items and furniture constructed from newspaper rolls. The pages themselves became part of the visual character of the building. Some of the surviving material offers a glimpse into the period. Reports about contemporary events, advertisements and newspaper headlines remain caught between layers of paper. The house therefore contains two kinds of history: the story of Stenman's experiment and the stories that were printed on the material he used.By the time the project had developed into its fuller form, almost every part of the interior that could be adapted to paper had been drawn into the idea. The frame and other elements that needed conventional construction remained, but newspaper had taken over an extraordinary amount of the visible space.The longevity of the building can make the experiment sound simpler than it was. Paper remains vulnerable to water, and it is combustible. The varnish protected against moisture, but it did not transform newspaper into a material with all the properties of brick, timber or other conventional building products. This is one of the important points behind the house's survival. It was not newspaper alone that lasted for more than a century. The wooden framework continued to provide the structural support, while the paper was layered, bonded and protected. The experiment also gained a second life after Stenman's work was completed. The house eventually became a museum, preserving not only the unusual construction method but the pages themselves. As the outer layers age and deteriorate, newer fragments underneath can become visible, revealing pieces of printed material that had been hidden for decades.There is something unusually literal about that process. A newspaper normally has a very short useful life. It is printed, read and discarded, often within a day. Inside the Rockport house, the same material became part of a building that outlived the people who had first read those pages. Finding new uses for paper, cardboard and cellulose fibres once their original purpose has ended. Modern materials made from such fibres are developed to meet very different technical requirements, particularly around moisture, strength and fire resistance. Stenman's house was a much more personal and improvised experiment.Still, its walls remain a physical reminder of what happens when an everyday material is treated differently. In 1922, old newspapers were gathered for an engineer's unusual building project. Decades later, the house contained not only newspaper walls but paper furniture and objects, while the wooden frame quietly continued doing the structural work beneath it. More than 100,000 newspapers became part of that experiment, turning something designed to be read briefly into a material that has remained in place for generations.
Article Summary: Elis F. Stenman began building a summer house in Rockport, Massachusetts, in 1922. More than 100,000 newspapers were used to build the house, with flour- based glue holding layers together and varnish helping protect them from moisture. The house came to contain newspaper tables, chairs, lamps, shelves and clocks.

Article Title: Missing former acting US attorney found dead in San Diego federal building; no foul play suspected
Article Text:
Andrew Haden was reported missing on Wednesday and was found dead hours later inside an office.

Found hours after being reported missing

‘One of the darkest days’

Who was Andrew Haden?

The search for a missing former acting US attorney in San Diego ended tragically after he was found dead inside a federal building, authorities said. No foul play is suspected, while the cause and manner of his death remain under investigation.Andrew Haden, 48, was reported missing on Wednesday and was found dead hours later inside an office at the Edward J. Schwartz Federal Building in downtown San Diego, according to the New York Post.A spokesperson said San Diego Police Department investigators responded to the scene “out of an abundance of caution” and found no indication of foul play.“The official cause and manner of death will be determined by the Medical Examiner,” the spokesperson said.Haden joined the US attorney’s office in 2010 and served twice as acting US attorney for the Southern District of California during leadership transitions, holding the role for roughly two months each in 2023 and 2025.Southern District US Attorney Adam Gordon mourned Haden’s death, describing Thursday as “one of the darkest days in our office’s history.”“But there was nothing dark about Andrew Haden’s life,” Gordon said, calling him “a beacon of light” known for his laughter, friendship, integrity and commitment to serving the community.Gordon later met with staff and informed employees about Haden’s death, according to the San Diego Union-Tribune.Further details were not disclosed out of respect for Haden’s wife and children.Raised in San Diego, Haden attended University City High before earning a bachelor’s degree in political science from Stanford University.He later served for five years in the Navy, including two overseas deployments, before attending the University of San Diego School of Law.He also worked as a law clerk for US District Judge Thomas J Whelan in the Southern District of California.Southern District of California Chief Judge Cynthia Bashant described his death as “a loss for everyone,” while defence attorney Jeremy Warren, who had faced Haden in court, said his death was “a huge blow to the entire federal community in San Diego.”
Article Summary: Andrew Haden, 48, was reported missing on Wednesday and was found dead hours later inside an office at the Edward J Schwartz Federal Building in downtown San Diego. No foul play is suspected, while the cause and manner of his death remain under investigation. Haden served twice as acting US attorney for the Southern District of California during leadership transitions.

Article Title: Imran Khan's kin say Pak govt violated court order for not taking ex-PM to private hospital
Article Text:
Imran Khan shifted back to jail after medical examination

Family alleges violation of court order

NEW DELHI: Former Pakistan PM Imran Khan was shifted back to Adiala Jail in Rawalpindi early Friday, hours after he was taken for a medical examination amid a legal battle over his health and demands from his family and supporters for better medical care.Khan, 73, was taken to the state-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) in Islamabad, Pakistan's information minister Attaullah Tarar said, news agaency PTI reports. The government later said Khan was medically fit and returned him to jail at around 5 am.The development came days after the Supreme Court ordered authorities to move Khan to Al-Shifa hospital following a medical report that said he was suffering from “level three plus” anxiety.Khan's family has repeatedly raised concerns about his access to adequate medical treatment while in custody. His sister, Uzma Khan, was present during the medical examination at PIMS, according to AP. They have accused authorities of violating a court order by taking him to a government hospital for a medical examination instead of a private hospital designated by the court.She alleged that during their meeting, Khan complained of being kept in solitary confinement, which she described as “mental torture” for the former prime minister.Khan’s personal physician, Faisal Sultan, said he had been taken to Shifa International Hospital, where he waited for Khan until early Friday. He was later informed that Khan had instead been returned to Adiala prison in Rawalpindi.Tarar said authorities changed the plan because of security concerns after supporters of Khan’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) gathered outside Shifa International Hospital or were heading there.Khan has been in custody since his arrest on August 5, 2023, in a corruption case.
Article Summary: Imran Khan, 73, was taken to the state-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) in Islamabad. The government later said Khan was medically fit and returned him to jail at around 5 am. The development came days after the Supreme Court ordered authorities to move Khan to Al-Shifa hospital.

Article Title: Ex-Pak PM Imran Khan moved to private hospital from prison after SC order
Article Text:
Imran Khan’s transfer follows months of health concerns, including a dispute over worsening vision in his right eye

Imprisoned former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan was shifted from Adiala prison to a private hospital in Islamabad after midnight Thursday for a medical examination, news agency AP reported citing Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party's statement.Khan was taken to Shifa International Hospital hours after Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry said the government would comply with a Supreme Court order directing authorities to facilitate his medical examination.The PTI said the transfer was carried out following the Supreme Court's order earlier this week but did not provide further details. It remained unclear whether Khan would return to prison after the examination or stay at the hospital for further treatment. His family and party have sought permission for him to remain there.Earlier Thursday, Chaudhry said the government had approached the Supreme Court seeking clarification on whether the medical relief granted to Khan applied only to him or could also cover other prisoners. He stressed that the request was not aimed at delaying or defying the court's order.The three-judge Supreme Court panel had ordered authorities two days earlier to take Khan to Shifa International Hospital for a medical examination amid prolonged concerns raised by his family and personal doctors over his health and access to treatment.The court directed that a medical board examine him, including specialists and his personal physician, Faisal Sultan.The government has maintained that prisoners receive medical care under existing rules and can be moved to government hospitals when required.Concerns over Khan's health intensified in January after his family claimed he had lost about 85% of the vision in his right eye. The government disputed the claim and later said his vision had improved by around 70%.Khan, a former cricket star, was ousted as prime minister in a parliamentary no-confidence vote in April 2022. He has remained imprisoned since 2023 after convictions in multiple cases, including a graft case.
Article Summary: Imran Khan was moved from Adiala prison to a private hospital in Islamabad after midnight Thursday for a medical examination. It remained unclear whether Khan would return to prison after the examination or stay at the hospital for further treatment. His family and party have sought permission for him to remain there. Khan, a former cricket star, was ousted as prime minister in a parliamentary no- confidence vote in April 2022.

Article Title: Red-faced Pakistan summons top diplomat over US envoy Gor's J&K remark in Srinagar
Article Text:
US Ambassador Sergio Gor visits Srinagar with J&K CM Omar

Pakistan on Wednesday summoned the top US diplomat Islamabad and lodged a protest after US envoy to India Sergio Gor described Jammu and Kashmir as an “important part of India” during his visit to Srinagar on Wednesday.The remarks came as Gor made his first visit to Jammu and Kashmir since taking office and met chief minister Omar Abdullah.Gor’s comments were made during a joint media briefing with Abdullah following their meeting at the chief minister’s residence. “It’s a pleasure to be here. This is an important part of India. I am here, visiting for the first time. It is an incredibly beautiful place. I am thrilled to be here,” the US envoy said.Gor also indicated that Washington could reconsider its travel advisory for Jammu and Kashmir, saying the US regularly reviews its warnings. He said the Indian government and the Jammu and Kashmir administration had taken steps to improve safety in the region.“I cannot make any big announcements here today, but it is something we are going to look at,” Gor said, adding that the US would consider whether its existing travel warning should be downgraded.The ambassador also described his meeting with Abdullah as “very good” and said the two sides had discussed ways to deepen economic cooperation and create opportunities benefiting India and the US.Abdullah said the talks focused on what Washington could do for Jammu and Kashmir, while also referring to “certain legacy issues” that would need to be addressed.“We look forward to taking this conversation further,” Abdullah said, adding that he was “very hopeful and optimistic” that engagement between the US and Jammu and Kashmir would “both widen and deepen in the years ahead”.
Article Summary: Pakistan summons top US diplomat Islamabad and lodges a protest. US envoy to India Sergio Gor described Jammu and Kashmir as an “important part of India’ Gor also indicated that Washington could reconsider its travel advisory for J&K.

Article Title: Pakistan govt to challenge SC order to move jailed ex-PM Imran Khan to hospital
Article Text:
'Not within four walls of law': Pak law minister on Khan hospitalisation order

The Shehbaz Sharif-led Pakistan government will challenge the Supreme Court's order directing the transfer of jailed former prime minister Imran Khan to a private hospital, as law minister Azam Nazeer Tarar confirmed in a video message on Wednesday.According to news agency Reuters, the Pakitan Supreme Court had ordered the government to move Khan to Islamabad’s Shifa International Hospital within two days and allow him access to his personal physician.“This order is not within four walls of the law,” Tarar said in a video statement.He said authorities had reviewed the ruling and decided to approach the court seeking a review. “A convicted prisoner has to be treated either inside the jail or at a public hospital according to law,” Tarar said, adding that the review petition would seek a modification of the order.The move could end hopes of Imran Khan’s family and Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), which have repeatedly sought better healthcare and visitation rights for the former PM.It could also trigger public discontent over his treatment in custody.Recently, Imran Khan supporters staged widespread protest over his imprisonment against Islamabad government.Khan, 73, has been jailed in Rawalpindi since August 2023 after being convicted in several cases that he says are politically motivated.He was removed from office in 2022 after falling out with Pakistan's powerful military establishment under army chief Asim Munir's influence.The Supreme Court order came after former president Arif Alvi raised concerns over World Cup winning captain and former PM's medical condition.Alvi also shared Khan's vitals on X.Imran Khan's sons have also repeatedly expressed concern about his deteriorating health, while his lawyers have claimed he suffered significant vision loss in his right eye while in prison.
Article Summary: Pakistani law minister Azam Nazeer Tarar confirms government will challenge the Supreme Court's order. Khan, 73, has been jailed in Rawalpindi since August 2023 after being convicted in several cases. He was removed from office in 2022 after falling out with Pakistan's powerful military establishment.

Article Title: Imran Khan’s sister meets him after 9 months as Pakistan SC orders hospital transfer for jailed ex-PM
Article Text:
Former Pak PM is set to be shifted to a hospital after top court's order over health concerns

Former Pakistan prime minister Imran Khan ’s sister Noreen Niazi met him at Rawalpindi's Adiala Jail on Tuesday after a gap of around nine months, following a Supreme Court order allowing weekly meetings between the former prime minister and his family amid concerns over his health.The meeting lasted around 15 minutes, according to jail sources, cited by Express Tribune. Noreen briefed Imran on the Supreme Court’s order regarding his transfer to Islamabad’s Shifa International Hospital and enquired about his health. The two also discussed ongoing legal matters.Noreen confirmed after the meeting that she had met her brother but did not speak to the media, in line with an assurance given before the court. She later left Adiala Jail with her sisters Aleema Khan and Uzma Khan.Imran also met his wife, Bushra Bibi, with their meeting lasting around 30-35 minutes. Bushra earlier met her daughter, Mubashra Sheikh, and sister-in-law Mehrunnisa.Before entering the jail, Noreen told reporters that she would inform Imran that “the Supreme Court has granted you permission” to meet his family. She also said she would brief him about efforts made by PTI workers on his behalf.The meetings followed a three-member Supreme Court bench headed by Justice Shahid Waheed directing the government to facilitate weekly meetings between Imran and his family. The court was hearing petitions concerning his access to his sisters and personal physicians, as well as his medical condition.The order came after a medical board report and a report by the Adiala Jail superintendent were submitted to the court. The reports recommended more frequent meetings with Imran’s immediate family and spouse to help manage his blood pressure and anxiety.The Supreme Court also ordered that Imran be moved to Shifa International Hospital for treatment and directed the formation of a medical board comprising an eye specialist, general physician, cardiologist and his personal physician, Dr Faisal Sultan. Dr Uzma was also to be included in the board.The court ordered that his medical records remain confidential and barred political activity or media interactions outside the hospital. It also directed authorities to arrange telephone contact between Imran and his children.Justice Waheed stressed that access to family could not be treated as a favour, describing the meetings as a fundamental right rather than a concession. The court, however, required PTI representatives to refrain from political activity or media engagement after meeting Imran, a condition the party said it would follow.Aleema Khan welcomed the order, saying the family had been demanding hospital treatment for Imran for months. Speaking to reporters at the Dahgal checkpoint in Rawalpindi, she said she was happy about the meeting but remained uncertain about whether the development signalled a broader change in circumstances.“"Words cannot describe how happy I am about the meeting. I cannot even imagine where I would have got sweets from. I have appeared before the ATC Rawalpindi from the Supreme Court,” Aleema said.She also rejected suggestions that the family was politicising Imran’s health, saying they were speaking as his sisters.PTI spokesperson Niazullah Khan Niazi said Imran had a right to meet his family twice a week but that authorities had continued to restrict access despite an Islamabad High Court order. He said the party would comply with the Supreme Court’s direction against political statements after meetings.Concerns over Imran’s health have intensified in recent months. A medical report submitted to the Supreme Court said he had experienced fluctuating blood pressure, palpitations, headaches, restlessness and significant anxiety.A PIMS cardiologist who examined him on August 1 recorded his blood pressure at 140/100mmHg and recommended measures to reduce mental stress, including more frequent meetings with his wife and access to reading material. A four-member medical board that examined him on August 10 recorded his blood pressure at 140/80mmHg and recommended walking, relaxation and more frequent interaction with his immediate family and spouse.The report said Imran had undergone at least 39 medical check-ups since his incarceration, with jail medical officers examining him three times a day. It also said his ECG was normal and his vision had improved to almost normal following treatment for an eye condition.PTI has questioned the authenticity and completeness of the medical documentation and demanded examinations by Imran’s personal physicians, Dr Asim Yusuf and Dr Faisal Sultan, as well as an independent medical board. The government has rejected claims that he is being denied proper medical care, saying he is receiving treatment from specialists in accordance with the law and court orders.A report submitted to the Supreme Court in February had said Imran’s right eye was functioning at only 15% capacity. The court subsequently ordered that he be granted access to his personal physicians in Adiala Jail.Imran and Bushra Bibi remain incarcerated at Adiala Jail in Rawalpindi. They were sentenced in December 2025 to 17 years in prison in the Toshakhana-II case over allegations that they unlawfully retained a Bulgari jewellery set gifted by the Saudi crown prince.Imran has been in custody since August 2023, initially following his conviction in the £190 million corruption case. He also faces pending trials under Pakistan’s Anti-Terrorism Act in connection with the May 9, 2023, protests.Imran, who served as prime minister from 2018 until his ouster through a parliamentary no-confidence vote in 2022, and his supporters have consistently maintained that the cases against him are politically motivated and aimed at preventing his political comeback.
Article Summary: Imran's sister Noreen Niazi met him at Rawalpindi's Adiala Jail on Tuesday after a gap of around nine months. Meeting followed a Supreme Court order allowing weekly meetings between the former prime minister and his family amid concerns over his health.

Article Title: 'Move Imran Khan to hospital': Pakistan Supreme Court directs govt amid ex-PM's health concerns
Article Text:
Pakistan SC orders Imran Khan’s hospital transfer. photo credit: AP

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you believe Imran Khan should receive immediate medical attention? Yes, he needs immediate care No, he can stay in jail Unsure, need more information 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Pakistan’s Supreme Court on Tuesday directed the government to move imprisoned former prime minister Imran Khan to a hospital, meeting a longstanding demand from his party and family amid growing concerns over his health.Khan, 73, has been in jail since August 2023 after being convicted in several cases that he and his supporters have described as politically motivated. His Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party welcomed the court order, saying it should have come earlier.“It’s a very welcome order and we wish it had happened sooner so his eye and general health would not have deteriorated this much,” PTI spokesperson Zulfikar Bukhari told Reuters.“He should remain in hospital until all doctors are satisfied,” Bukhari added.According to Khan’s spokesperson Naeem Haider Panjutha, the court directed that he be moved to Shifa International Hospital within 48 hours and remain there until September 16.Also Read: 'Needs to be moved to hospital now': Imran Khan's health in jail deteriorates The order came amid renewed concerns over Khan’s physical and mental health. His sons, Sulaiman Khan and Kasim Khan, have repeatedly raised concerns about his access to family, lawyers and doctors.“We have no updates because his family, doctors and lawyers haven’t been allowed to see him for seven months,” they told CNN earlier this month.The development came after former Pakistani president Arif Alvi also said on Tuesday that Khan’s medical reports were “alarming”, citing concerns over anxiety, palpitations and high blood pressure.In a post on X, Alvi said, “Imran Khan’s medical reports are alarming. I have gone through them with several specialists, and I am writing this in plain language so every Pakistani can understand exactly what is happening.”Alvi said the issues that concerned him most were Khan’s “anxiety and stress levels”, “palpitations,” and “high blood pressure”.Alvi also raised concerns over Khan’s heart rate and called for further medical monitoring, including a 24-hour Holter monitor.“I am deeply worried. Isolation is taking a physical toll on his body. If this is not addressed immediately, the damage may become irreversible with more complications to follow,” Alvi said.Calling for Khan to be hospitalised, the former president said: “@ImranKhanPTI definitely needs to be moved to a hospital environment now, under an independent panel of doctors.”Khan’s legal troubles intensified after his ouster as prime minister in a no-confidence vote in 2022. He has faced multiple cases, including those involving state gifts and an unlawful marriage, with some convictions suspended or overturned and appeals pending. He denies wrongdoing.The PTI, which came to power in 2018 and retains a significant support base, was stripped of its election symbol before the 2024 general election, forcing its candidates to contest as independents.
Article Summary: Pakistan's Supreme Court orders former prime minister Imran Khan to be moved to a hospital. Khan has been in jail since August 2023 after being convicted in several cases. His party welcomed the court order, saying it should have come earlier. The order came amid renewed concerns over Khan’s physical and mental health.

Article Title: 'Needs to be moved to hospital now': Imran Khan's health in jail deteriorates
Article Text:
Alvi warns over Imran Khan’s worsening health

NEW DELHI: Former Pakistan President Arif Alvi on Tuesday raised the alarm over jailed ex-PM Imran Khan’s worsening health, saying his medical reports were “alarming” and pointing to anxiety, heart palpitations and high blood pressure.In a post on X, Alvi said, "Imran Khan's medical reports are alarming. I have gone through them with several specialists, and I am writing this in plain language so every Pakistani can understand exactly what is happening."Alvi said the issues that concerned him most were Khan's "anxiety and stress levels", "palpitations," and "high blood pressure." He added that while sleeplessness was not mentioned in the report, Khan's medication appeared to suggest the problem."I have known Imran Khan for more than 35 years. Stress was never his weakness. That it is now at peak levels tells you everything about what three years of imprisonment and total isolation have done to him," he said.Alvi attributed Khan's stress to the political situation in Pakistan, the imprisonment and deaths of his colleagues, his own prolonged isolation and limited access to newspapers, books and information from outside.He also raised concerns over former PM and the only world-cup winning cricket captain Imran Khan's heart rate, which he said had increased to 54 beats per minute (bpm), compared with his historically lower resting rate."His heart rate is 54 bpm. Doctors will call that 'normal.' It is not normal for him," Alvi said, adding that Khan had also reported heart palpitations.Alvi called for Khan to undergo immediate cardiac monitoring, saying he "needs a 24-hour Holter monitor immediately". He also urged regular monitoring of his blood pressure.He recommended several tests, including a stress test, echocardiogram, cardiac MRI, cardiac artery calcium scan and cardiac CT angiogram, along with any other tests doctors may consider necessary."I am deeply worried. Isolation is taking a physical toll on his body. If this is not addressed immediately, the damage may become irreversible with more complications to follow," Alvi said.Calling for Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf founder Khan to be shifted to a hospital, Alvi said, "Imran Khan definitely needs to be moved to a hospital environment now, under an independent panel of doctors.""Neither his family nor the people of Pakistan trust government-appointed doctors alone," he added."The next three months will decide whether his condition is reversed or becomes permanent," Alvi said. He further said, "We all are alarmed. The country needs him more than ever before."Khan remains behind bars, while his sons, Sulaiman Khan and Kasim Khan, have also raised concerns about their father's access to his family, lawyers and doctors."We have no updates because his family, doctors and lawyers haven't been allowed to see him for seven months," they told CNN earlier this month.The statements came amid nationwide demonstrations by supporters of Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), who have demanded the release of the former prime minister and his wife, Bushra Bibi.Khan served as Pakistan's prime minister from 2018 until his ouster through a parliamentary no-confidence vote in 2022. He has been imprisoned since 2023 following convictions in several cases, including graft charges and the alleged disclosure of official secrets.Khan and his political aides have consistently alleged that the cases against him are politically motivated and intended to prevent his return to politics.After his ouster, Khan led nationwide rallies alleging that the government of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had conspired with Pakistan's military establishment and Washington to remove him. The subsequent crackdown targeted PTI leaders and supporters, while the party was barred from contesting the 2024 general elections.Khan's supporters have repeatedly maintained that the legal proceedings against him are politically motivated and aimed at blocking his political comeback.
Article Summary: Former Pakistan President Arif Alvi raises alarm over jailed ex-PM Imran Khan’s worsening health. Alvi says Khan's medical reports were “alarming” and pointed to anxiety, heart palpitations and high blood pressure. He also raised concerns over former PM's heart rate, which he said had increased to 54 beats per minute.

Article Title: '30 civilans killed': Baloch activist shares video of 'Pakistani war crime', seeks US intervention
Article Text:
Mir Yar Baloch has urged the US administration to impose sanctions on Pakistan.

Baloch leader seeks US sanctions

ALSO READ |

Pakistan disputes airstrike allegations

Protests erupt over reported civilian deaths

ALSO READ |

Mir Yar Baloch, a Baloch leader, has accused Pakistan 's military of carrying out an airstrike in Balochistan that allegedly killed 30 civilians, including women, children and infants.He claimed that video footage from the August 12 attack in Surab's Gidar Goandhan area provides evidence of the military operation and said he plans to take the matter to the International Criminal Court."The Republic of Balochistan has obtained video footage of the Surab Air Strike conducted by the external terrorist forces of Pakistan on 12th August, which killed 30 innocent Balochistan civilians including women, children, and infants and injured dozens more. The missile debris clearly visible in the video constitute irrefutable proof of Pakistan's terrorism. They also thoroughly expose Pakistan's military spokesperson, DG ISPR, who deliberately misled the global community on national media by claiming the attack was merely an IED blast on the ground," Mir Yar Baloch wrote on X.Mir Yar Baloch has urged the US administration to impose sanctions on Pakistan and halt military support, including F-16 engine spare parts and upgrades to fighter jets and missile programmes."The Republic of Balochistan urges the Trump administration to impose strict economic sanctions on Pakistan, cancel the delivery of spare parts for F-16 engines, and halt all upgradation package to its fighter jets and missile program.The Pakistan military and air force are massively employing these very weapons and aircraft against the people of the independent Republic of Balochistan. Washington must hold Pakistan fully accountable for its war crimes in Balochistan," he added.The two sides have given sharply different accounts of what happened in Surab, leaving the circumstances of the incident and the actual civilian death toll disputed.Pakistan's military has rejected the claim of an airstrike and said the casualties were caused by a premature explosion involving a vehicle-borne improvised explosive device allegedly being assembled by militants.The Inter-Services Public Relations said the initial blast killed eight militants and that a secondary explosion involving other explosives stored at the site also caused civilian deaths."However, the blast and secondary detonation of other explosives stored there by the terrorists of Indian Proxy have also reportedly caused tragic casualties of three nearby civilians," the ISPR said.The military said Pakistani forces and Balochistan Police subsequently killed 10 more individuals, taking the reported militant death toll to 18. Two Pakistani soldiers were also injured during the exchange of fire.The competing accounts have come amid protests in Balochistan following reports of civilian deaths in the Surab area.The Balochistan Post reported that more than 20 people were initially killed and at least 16 injured in the incident. Some local residents, however, claimed that the actual death toll could be higher.
Article Summary: Baloch leader Mir Yar Baloch has accused Pakistan's military of carrying out an airstrike in Balochistan that allegedly killed 30 civilians. He claims that video footage from the August 12 attack in Surab's Gidar Goandhan area provides evidence of the military operation. He has urged the US administration to impose sanctions on Pakistan.

Article Title: Pakistani minister in Balochistan province escapes armed attack on convoy
Article Text:
All six injured people suffered bullet wounds, according to a senior police official.​

Balochistan home minister Mir Ziaullah Langove escaped unharmed after armed attackers targeted his convoy in Mastung district on Friday, injuring six people, including three police personnel.The attack took place in the Khad Kocha area as Langove was travelling from Quetta to Kalat, Balochistan government spokesperson Shahid Rind said."Six people were injured in the attack, but the minister remained unhurt and the convoy has returned to Quetta," Rind said.All six injured people suffered bullet wounds, according to a senior police official. Three of them were police personnel, with two reportedly in serious condition. They were taken to a hospital in Quetta for treatment.The attack has raised fresh security concerns in Khad Kocha, an area that has repeatedly come under attack in recent weeks.According to officials, this was the fourth attack on travellers along the same highway since last month. Insurgents have repeatedly targeted people travelling through the area despite a major security operation carried out following the earlier incidents.Security forces have now sealed off the area and launched a search operation to locate those responsible for the latest attack.The incident adds to the continuing security challenges in Balochistan, where armed insurgent groups have carried out attacks against security forces and civilians.
Article Summary: Balochistan home minister Mir Ziaullah Langove escaped unharmed after armed attackers targeted his convoy. The attack took place in the Khad Kocha area as Langove was travelling from Quetta to Kalat. All six injured people suffered bullet wounds, according to a senior police official.

Article Title: 'Water is our red line': Shehbaz Sharif threatens India with 'direct response' over Indus Treaty
Article Text:
Shehbaz Sharif speaking on eve of Pakistan's Independence Day

Poll Vote & Share your view Should the Indus Waters Treaty be renegotiated? Yes, it needs changes No, it should remain unchanged 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Pakistan has yet again raked up India’s suspension of the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT), with its Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif threatening a “direct response” to New Delhi’s move, which came days after the Pahalgam terror attack in Jammu and Kashmir in April last year."The Prime Minister said that India has proven itself an enemy of peace by unilaterally and illegally suspending the Indus Waters Treaty. He announced that every drop of Pakistan's water is our red line. There will be no compromise on the water issue. If India does not come to the right path, we will give it a direct response," the Pakistan Prime Minister's Office said in a statement on X.Sharif, speaking at an event on the eve of Pakistan’s Independence Day (August 14), sought to portray India as an “enemy of peace” over New Delhi’s decision to keep the IWT in abeyance following the April 22 Pahalgam terror attack, in which 26 civilians were killed.He said New Delhi had proved itself an “enemy” of peace by putting the treaty in abeyance."India proved itself an enemy of peace by unilaterally and illegally suspending the Indus Waters Treaty. I declare in clear terms that every single drop of Pakistan's water is our red line. If India does not come to its senses, it will be responded to directly," the Pakistani premier added.The military hostilities ended on May 10 after Islamabad sought a ceasefire following India’s air strikes on multiple Pakistani air bases.The conflict erupted after India's Operation Sindoor in retaliation for the Pahalgam attack.New Delhi kept the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance after a Cabinet Committee on Security (CCS) meeting on April 23, 2025, and asserted that the conditions under which the treaty was negotiated have "fundamentally changed."India has asserted the treaty can no longer function in its present form and will remain in abeyance until Pakistan “credibly and irrevocably” ends its support for cross-border terrorism.The Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) was signed in September 1960.
Article Summary: Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif threatens a "direct response" to India's suspension of the Indus Waters Treaty. The move came days after the Pahalgam terror attack in Jammu and Kashmir in April last year. New Delhi kept the IWT in abeyance after a Cabinet Committee on Security meeting on April 23, 2025.

Article Title: Why US is questioning Pakistan's Rs 3 trillion defence spending
Article Text:
The US also criticised Islamabad for not publishing its executive budget proposal within a reasonable period (representative image)

US asks Pakistan to improve defence and debt transparency

Pakistan's defence allocation rises to Rs 3 trillion

Defence spending remains a key transparency concern

The US state department has flagged a lack of adequate parliamentary and civilian oversight of Pakistan's military and intelligence spending, while also raising concerns over limited disclosure of government debt and delays in publishing the executive budget proposal.The concerns were highlighted in the 2026 Fiscal Transparency Report, which assessed Pakistan's public financial transparency and identified gaps in the country's budgetary and fiscal disclosure practices.The report noted that Pakistan made its enacted budget and end-of-year financial statements widely available online. However, it said military and intelligence budgets remained outside adequate parliamentary or civilian public scrutiny.“The military and intelligence budgets were not subject to adequate parliamentary or civilian public oversight,” the report said.The US also criticised Islamabad for not publishing its executive budget proposal within a reasonable period.According to the assessment, this limits the time available for lawmakers and civil society to examine government spending before the budget is adopted.The state department called for three key changes to Pakistan's fiscal transparency framework.It urged Islamabad to make its executive budget proposal publicly available within a reasonable period, disclose detailed information about government debt obligations, including liabilities linked to state-owned enterprises, and bring military and intelligence agency budgets under parliamentary or civilian public oversight.The report also raised concerns about Pakistan's disclosure of public debt, saying only limited information was available on debt obligations, including those of major state-owned enterprises.At the same time, the US assessment acknowledged some positive aspects of Pakistan's public financial system.It said the country's supreme audit institution met international standards of independence and noted that its audit reports were published in a timely manner and contained substantive findings.The US assessment comes against the backdrop of a substantial increase in Pakistan's defence allocation for the 2026-27 financial year.In June, Pakistan's federal government proposed allocating Rs 3 trillion for defence services, up 17.65 per cent from the previous year's initial allocation of Rs 2.55 trillion, according to Dawn.The proposed defence services allocation amounts to about 2.08 per cent of Pakistan's projected GDP of Rs 143.6 trillion and nearly 16 per cent of the federal government's total outlay of Rs 18.77 trillion.Spending on civil works related to military infrastructure was projected to rise 7.92 per cent to Rs 363.16 billion, from Rs 336.49 billion previously.Military pensions are accounted for separately from the main defence services budget. The government has allocated Rs 822 billion for retired military personnel under the federal pension outlay, according to Dawn.The allocation for defence administration was set at Rs 10.9 billion, compared with Rs 7.9 billion in the outgoing fiscal year's original budget. That allocation was later revised to Rs 11.75 billion.Major military imports and defence acquisitions are generally funded outside the main defence services allocation and remain undisclosed.The US state department's assessment therefore highlights a distinction between Pakistan's publicly disclosed defence allocation and the wider military spending that may not be fully visible through the country's budgetary documents.The state department's recommendations focus on bringing military and intelligence expenditure into the broader framework of public financial oversight.While the report recognised that Pakistan publishes key budget documents, it identified defence and intelligence spending, debt disclosure and the timing of budget publication as areas requiring greater transparency.The recommendations would require Pakistan to give lawmakers and the public greater visibility into military and intelligence allocations, as well as government liabilities linked to state-owned enterprises.
Article Summary: US asks Pakistan to improve defence and debt transparency. Pakistan's defence allocation rises to Rs 3 trillion for 2026-27 financial year. US state department flagged a lack of adequate parliamentary and civilian oversight of Pakistan's military and intelligence spending. Report also raised concerns over limited disclosure of government debt and delays in publishing executive budget proposal.

Article Title: PML-N set to form 'government' in PoK after two former 'premiers' lose strongholds in third phase
Article Text:
Two former PoK premiers lost their strongholds in the third phase of elections marred by violence and rigging allegations, as the PML-N emerged dominant

Two former so-called prime ministers of Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) lost their traditional strongholds in the third phase of elections, according to unofficial results released on Tuesday, while incumbent premier Faisal Mumtaz Rathore of the Pakistan People's Party (PPP) retained his seat.The latest results came after voting in four constituencies on Monday, with the election process again overshadowed by violence and allegations of rigging. Polling in the remaining seven constituencies was postponed over concerns about the law-and-order situation and is expected to be held on August 21, according to the region's election commission.The PPP won two of the four seats contested in the third phase, while the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) and the Awami Dast-o-Bazu Party won one each. The latter is backed by both Jamaat-e-Islami and Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI).Former prime minister and Muslim Conference president Sardar Attique Ahmed Khan, who was backed by the PML-N, lost the seat in Western Bagh's Dhirkot constituency to Awami Dast-o-Bazu Party candidate Sardar Sajid Iqbal, according to unofficial results. The seat had been held by the Muslim Conference/PML-N since 1985.In Central Bagh, PPP's Zia Qamar retained the seat, defeating PML-N candidate Mushtaq Minhas.Former premier Sardar Tanveer Ilyas, who joined the Istehkam-i-Pakistan Party, secured only a few thousand votes.The result in Eastern Bagh remained pending after authorities ordered a re-poll at 12 polling stations. PML-N candidate Sardar Mir Akbar was leading based on results from 174 of the constituency's 186 polling stations, followed by PPP candidate Sardar Qamaruz Zaman Khan.The election comes against the backdrop of a striking shift in the Pakistani government's treatment of the protest movement that has rocked PoK for months.Just days before the final phase of voting, Pakistan's defence minister Khawaja Asif had described the protesters as "enemies of Pakistan" and ruled out talks with them. But Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's adviser Rana Sanaullah subsequently said 99% of those associated with the Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) were "patriotic brothers", promising that a PML-N government would engage with the group and seek to resolve its demands.The reversal in rhetoric came as the PML-N emerged as the dominant force in the election and prepared to form the next government in the region. The party has secured 25 of the 45 directly elected seats so far, while the PPP has won 12 and the Awami Dast-o-Bazu Party one.The first two phases, held on July 27 and August 2, were also marked by violent protests and allegations of widespread rigging, with the PML-N and PPP accusing each other of electoral malpractice. Supporters of the two parties clashed at several polling stations.The JAAC has been protesting across the region since early June, with demands including the abolition of 12 refugee seats that it says can be used to influence the formation of governments in PoK.The group has alleged that more than 40 people were killed during violence surrounding the first phase of voting and that around 400 protesters had been killed since the protests began. The Pakistani government has rejected the higher figure as exaggerated, while Sanaullah has acknowledged that deaths from the unrest were in the "double figures".India does not recognise Pakistan's control over the territory, maintaining that Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh are integral and inalienable parts of India and describing Pakistan's presence in areas under its control as "illegal and forcible occupation".
Article Summary: Two former so-called prime ministers of Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) lost their traditional strongholds in the third phase of elections. Incumbent premier Faisal Mumtaz Rathore of the Pakistan People's Party (PPP) retained his seat. Polling in the remaining seven constituencies was postponed over concerns about the law-and-order situation.

Article Title: 'Discontent answered with bullets': MEA slams Pakistan over PoK crackdown
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs on Tuesday slammed Pakistan for its ongoing crackdown on protesters in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir, calling upon the international community to hold the country accountable for the "gross violation of human rights. "During the bi-weekly press briefing, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said that public discontent in PoK was answered with bullets and blackouts by authorities in Pakistan."We would like to highlight the human rights violations being committed in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir and other parts of the country. We call upon the international community to hold Pakistan accountable for its misdeeds, abuses and gross violations of human rights, including against its own people," Jaiswal said."Over the last several months, we have seen large-scale protests in PoK, including during and before the elections. Public discontent was answered with bullets, blackouts, repression and oppression. More than 90 people have been killed and many more injured. This has made news across the world," he added.Also Read | 'Arunachal is integral part of India, nothing can change this': MEA on China's fresh 'objections' The remarks came as at least 90 people, including protesters, security personnel and bystanders, were killed in clashes during June and July.The banned Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) has been staging protests in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) since June over the contentious 12 refugee seats. It has alleged that Pakistan's establishment manipulates these seats to install a prime minister of its choice to lead the so-called PoK government.Meanwhile, the third phase of elections in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) was held on Monday in four constituencies, amid violence and allegations of rigging. Polling started in Poonch Division’s Bagh and Haveli districts at 8 am, while elections in seven constituencies have been indefinitely postponed.Clashes between Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) and Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) workers were reported in some areas as the region's election commission classified most of the 803 polling stations as "sensitive or highly sensitive".After the first and second phases of polling, which were marred by violent protests and were held on July 27 and August 2, respectively, voting was scheduled for Monday in 11 constituencies of the Poonch Division in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir. There are 53 seats in the so-called PoK Legislative Assembly - 45 are directly elected, while eight are reserved for women, technocrats and clerics.The second phase of polling on August 2 was marred by violence and allegations of rigging. One person was killed and several others were injured.Also read | British national killed in PoK clashes; another held for over 2 months, says report The phase also included voting for the 12 refugee seats, which are at the centre of the ongoing controversy.Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) swept the second phase, winning 16 seats, while Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) secured the remaining five. In the first phase on July 27, PML-N won nine of the 13 seats, while PPP won four. With the first two phases combined, PML-N has already secured 24 seats.
Article Summary: MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said that public discontent in PoK was answered with bullets and blackouts by authorities in Pakistan. At least 90 people, including protesters, security personnel and bystanders, were killed in clashes during June and July. The banned Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) has been staging protests in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) since June.

Article Title: After weeks of violent protests, PoK votes in final election phase amid PTI, JAAC boycott calls
Article Text:
Pakistan’s elections were marked by protests and violence, raising concerns over security, political stability and the credibility of the electoral process.

Polling for Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir's so called assembly elections entered its final phase on Monday amid heightened security and reports of Islamabad-backed crackdown in the region.Voting is being held despite boycott calls from the Imran Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's (PTI) PoJK unit and the Pakistan-banned Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC).The tussle between the JAAC and the Shehbaz Sharif-Asim Munir duo's crackdown has made the situation grim in PoK.India has also strongly condemned the crackdown on protesters. The MEA has called the so-called assembly elections in the illegally occupied region as a "farce".The MEA also condemned Pakistan's actions that led to the killing of 90 civilians in PoK.Meanwhile, Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf’s (PTI) PoJK unit has announced a complete boycott of the ongoing electoral process in Pakistan-occupied Jammu & Kashmir (PoJK), calling it “unconstitutional” and “unfair”.The election has taken place against the backdrop of weeks of protests led by the JAAC, which has been demanding greater political rights for residents of Pakistan-occupied Kashmir.The final phase also came after media curbs, and other major restrictions imposed by Islamabad authority.The demonstrations have also seen clashes with security forces, overshadowing the election campaign.The ruling Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) has already secured a majority in the assembly, seeing a likely return after a decade.
Article Summary: Polling for Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir's so called assembly elections entered its final phase on Monday. Voting is being held despite boycott calls from the Imran Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's (PTI) PoJK unit and the Pakistan-banned Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) The election has taken place against the backdrop of weeks of protests.
